In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, 2521, 2530 and proposed Resolution No. 2534, due to the continuing state of
emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus,
this meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate virtually in the meeting
in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 9128) from any phone, Meeting ID:
830 9809 3007 Passcode: 569263. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the carolc@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m.
prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Planning Commission for their consideration and included
as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 830 9809 3007 Passcode: 569263.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are available on
the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 7, 2022

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:12 p.m. via teleconference pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  Low

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, OCTOBER 3, 2022

Administrative Analyst Corea noted an error in Item 7A.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE THE AMMENDED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 3, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220218: LOCAL EARLY ACTION PLANNING (LEAP)
  GRANT PROGRAM - SB 743 IMPLEMENTATION ADOPTING A NEW CEQA VEHICLE
  MILES TRAVELED (VMT) POLICY

Director Wahba stated introduced the city’s transportation consultant, John Muggridge with Fehr
& Peers.

John Muggridge, Fehr & Peers, provided a presentation on Planning Application No. PA-220218,
which included an overview of SB 743, and the implementation process; CEQA implications for
the city; and the non-CEQA components.

Director Wahba stated that Staff recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution
No. 220218, recommending to the City Council, adoption of a policy to comply with SB 743 and
CEQA requirements to establish vehicle miles traveled (VMT) as the metric used to determine the
CEQA-related transportation impacts of new development and transportation projects, and
determining that the adoption of the VMT policy is categorically exempt from CEQA.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 220218, RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL,
  ADOPTION OF A POLICY TO COMPLY WITH SB 743 AND CEQA REQUIREMENTS TO
  ESTABLISH VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED (VMT) AS THE METRIC USED TO
  DETERMINE THE CEQA-RELATED TRANSPORTATION IMPACTS OF NEW
  DEVELOPMENT AND TRANSPORTATION PROJECTS, AND DETERMINING THAT
  THE ADOPTION OF THE VMT POLICY IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM CEQA.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 7, 2022
  1
 AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Low
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission has approved the adoption of Resolution
no. 220218. Staff will present this item to the City Council for approval on Tuesday, November 8,
2022.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the improvements in the business district. Director
Wahba stated that there have been some issues with the contractor. Several ADA ramps are
being redesigned; staff is working with Rancho Palos Verdes on some of the trees that can either
be root pruned or removed from the islands to replace curb and gutter; and driveway apron repairs
are being added to the project. The pavement repair may be held off until after the first of the new
year.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Wahba introduced and welcomed back Jeannie Naughton, Community Development
Director.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – OCTOBER 11, 2022

CHAIR SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

 11.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:40 p.m.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Schachter, Chair
